newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Top Belgian stock brokers see more consolidation.
newsitem.headline: Top Belgian stock brokers see more consolidation.

text.p: Directors of Belgium's two biggest stock brokers said on Tuesday they expected further concentration in their sector as the brokerage industry prepared for the introduction of a single European currency in 1999.

"Competition in our industry is very strong, and we will see victims of that. The weakest links in the chain will disappear," Henri Servais, director of Brussels-based brokerage Dewaay Servais & Cie SA, told a seminar on the future of Brussels as a financial centre.
Servais said that already 10 percent of the brokerage houses were getting 80 percent of trading commissions from large institutional investors.
He said he thought competition in the industry would concentrate on two areas -- research and order execution.

"In the United States there are already brokers who work for zero commission and there are even some who propose paying (rather than being paid) for order execution so as to have a strong order flow and to be credible among institutional investors," Servais said.

Michel Peterbroeck, director of the other leading Brussels brokerage house, Petercam, told the seminar that the number of brokerages in Belgium had fallen to 56 in 1997 from 220 in 1987, and that the number was sure to shrink further by 2000.
He said that in an increasingly institutionalised market where commissions were tiny, brokers would fight for their survival by focusing on giving advice to their customers.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6810, Fax +32 2 230 7710
